note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/api/a2a.reason: cinatra#2567 (epic #2564 S3) conversational pull: FOUR new first-party modules become reachable from every locked route, because the app's auth plugins mount the MCP server — so an MCP capability module lands on all five graphs, not just /api/mcp. They are (1) src/lib/lifecycle/lifecycle-pull-mcp.ts, the three read-only pull primitives themselves; (2) src/lib/lifecycle/lifecycle-card-refetch.ts, S1's authorization ladder (run READ -> gate state -> decision axis) — reached rather than re-implemented, which is the whole point: a second copy of that ordering is exactly how a gate-existence leak gets introduced; (3) src/lib/assistant-runtime/lifecycle-view-envelope.ts, S1's producer, an import-free leaf and the only way to mint a card ref; (4) packages/agents/src/lifecycle-verification-read-store.ts, a NEW leaf this slice carves out. That fourth module is a NARROWING, not growth: reaching readVerificationRecordForGate through the verification WRITE store pulled its whole lane (the core-analysis lane, the advisory store and their app-side cores — EIGHT modules) onto all five routes just to answer 'is there a row?'. Splitting the read into its own leaf, with the write store re-exporting it so no caller changes, turns a measured +11 into this +4. No further narrowing is available without duplicating S1's ladder or its producer. Uniform +4 on every locked route, measured as a DELTA against this branch's merge base with the companion extension repos cloned, exactly as CI measures.
